text: {"score":4,"justification":"Numbers match the card and tool outputs (6.2x, 24.1% vs 3.9%, z 3.18, 37% low complexity, 30 charts, 0 of 7 below billed, audit-trail rates 13%/17%, 4 of 24 data without tests). Language is cautious ('rates, not proof', 'inconclusive'), and next steps are concrete. Weaknesses: the headline says 'Charts support the bill', which is stronger than the 7 documented 99215 claims warrant and sits oddly with the cautious leaning. The headline's 16% (the 0-condition share) is correct but peers 2.2% is actually the all-provider share. The 'Top priority' claims (C0108401, C0108297, C0108462) come from the audit-trail flags, yet the cited examples and next steps use different claims (C0108186, C0108260), so the flagged claims are not the ones cited or requested. C0108401 and C0108462 do not appear on the card. The 'against 14% for comparison providers' figure is grounded. It also doesn't note that the 4 supported 99215 examples include C0108297 and C0108298, which are low-complexity claims with high MDM documented, a notable tension left unexplored.","problems":["Headline 'Charts support the bill' overstates given only 7 documented 99215 claims and later 'inconclusive' leaning","Priority claims C0108401/C0108462 are not on the evidence card and not cited; the cited examples differ from the audit-flagged claims","Next step requests charts for C0108186 and C0108260 only, ignoring the audit-flagged claims and the low-complexity 99215 claims already documented as high MDM (C0108297, C0108298)","Summary is dense and repetitive, restating note-check rates twice","Missing results deficiency (MISSING_RESULTS) from the records exchange is not mentioned as a gap"]}
